problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A$, where

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}3{y}^{2},\, & \text{if}\,1<x<9,\,-1<y<1, \\ \frac{1}{4\sqrt{xy}},\, & \text{if}\,1<x<9,\,1<y<4,\end{aligned}
$$

and  $R$ is the domain of $f.$

examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Double Integral Using the Additivity Over a Rectangular Domain
examples.problem:
Evaluate the double integral $\displaystyle \iint\limits_{R}  f(x,y)\ \textrm d A$, where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14054242/assets/d96ec9ab40f8f1cadd6d2492dddcc0090f766b72e9c7fdb659e3b2f7f39fce0d.png)
and  $R$ is the domain of $f.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that we have $R = R_1 \cup R_2,$ where $R_1= (0,2) \times (-1,0)$ and $R_2= (0,2) \times (0,1).$ So, we can write

$$
\eqalign{
\iint\limits_{R}  f(x,y)\ \textrm d A &= \iint\limits_{R_1} 2 \ \textrm d A + \iint\limits_{R_2}    \dfrac{1}{xy+x+y+1} \ \textrm d A\[5pt]
&= 2\iint\limits_{R_1} \textrm d A
+ \iint\limits_{R_2}  \dfrac{1}{(x+1)(y+1)} \ \textrm d A\[5pt]
&= 2(2-0)(0-(-1)) + \Bigg( \int_0^2 \dfrac{1}{x+1} \ \textrm d x \Bigg) \Bigg( \int_0^1 \dfrac{1}{y+1}\ \textrm d y \Bigg) \[5pt]
&= 4 + \Big[\ln(x+1)\Big]_0^2  \cdot \Big[\ln(y+1)\Big]_0^1\[5pt] 
&= 4+ \ln 3\ln 2.
}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the domain $R$ can be represented as a union of three sub-domains, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =S\cup T\cup U.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{S}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{T}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{S}x\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{T}0\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{S}x\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{U}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$
